details: The U.S. Treasury Department has announced the freezing of over $344 million in cryptocurrency linked to Iran. This action is part of "Operation Economic Fury," an ongoing campaign designed to cripple Iran's financial lifelines by targeting its ability to generate, move, and repatriate funds globally, including through digital assets. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that Iran's key oil export hub is nearing a breaking point due to these pressures. This move signals an expansion of U.S. sanctions into digital financial channels, aiming to disrupt funding mechanisms outside conventional banking systems.
title: US Freezes $344M in Iranian Crypto Amid Sanctions Push

details: Iranian authorities and individuals are increasingly using cryptocurrencies as an alternative channel to circumvent international sanctions. This includes using digital assets to preserve savings amidst currency depreciation and restricted access to global banking systems. The U.S. is actively working to counter these evasion tactics, leading to a "cat-and-mouse game" in the digital finance realm. Data indicates Iran's crypto activity exceeded $7.7 billion last year, with users shifting to self-custodied wallets during periods of geopolitical risk.
title: How Iran Uses Crypto to Evade Sanctions, US Counter-Efforts
